chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Wine is from five: the juice pressed from the vine, the infusion of raisins, the mead from honey, the ale from barley, and the Nabeez from dates.'

key_terms.النَّبِيذُ: A specific type of fermented date drink
key_terms.النَّقِيعُ: Infusion or maceration (of raisins in water)

ai.seo_question: What are the five sources of wine (khamr) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi provides the definitive classification of the five primary sources of khamr, establishing the material basis for the prohibition of intoxicants in Shia jurisprudence. By linking these specific ingredients to the Prophet, it reinforces the concept that fermentation from these bases renders a drink impure and prohibited, a principle central to the works of later scholars like al-Tusi and al-Majlisi.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The wine is from five – the grape juice, and the marinade of the raisins, and the mead from the honey, and the ale from the barley, and Al-Nabeez from the dates’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from af-Fadf ibn Shadhan from all ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajj aj who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
Intoxicating liquors are made from five kinds of substances: grape juice, extracts of raisins, al-Bit’ (mead) from honey, al-Mizru (beer) from barley and wine from dates.”’
